subject: history
topicDisplay: Prescribed Subject Military Leaders Conquest Its Impact Move To Global War Rights Protest Diplomatic Crises
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which years was the Korean War fought?
questions.explain: The Korean War lasted from 1950 to the armistice of 1953.

questions.q: The National Origins (Johnson-Reed) Immigration Act, which set strict national quotas, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The 1924 Immigration Act established national-origin quotas that heavily favoured northern and western Europeans.

questions.q: In which year did Fascist Italy invade Abyssinia (Ethiopia)?
questions.explain: Italy invaded Abyssinia in October 1935, completing its conquest in 1936 and provoking League of Nations sanctions.

questions.q: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis occur?
questions.explain: The Cuban Missile Crisis unfolded in October 1962, the closest the superpowers came to nuclear war.

questions.q: In which year did Pope Urban II preach the sermon at Clermont that launched the First Crusade?
questions.explain: Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in November 1095.

questions.q: The Tennessee Valley Authority, a key New Deal agency providing electricity and flood control, was created in which year?
questions.explain: The TVA was established in 1933 as part of FDR's First New Deal.

questions.q: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, bringing the USA into the Second World War, took place on which date?
questions.explain: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, prompting the US declaration of war.

questions.q: The 1929 agreement that reconciled the Fascist state with the papacy was known as the:
questions.explain: The Lateran Pacts of 1929 recognised Vatican City as an independent state and settled the long-standing 'Roman Question'.

questions.q: Which two reform policies are most associated with Gorbachev?
questions.explain: Gorbachev pursued glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring).

questions.q: Which 1979 event helped trigger the 'Second Cold War'?
options: The fall of the Berlin Wall
questions.explain: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979 ended detente and heightened tensions.

questions.q: Franklin D. Roosevelt was first elected President of the United States in which year?
questions.explain: FDR won the 1932 presidential election and launched the New Deal after his March 1933 inauguration.

questions.q: The Social Security Act, introducing federal old-age pensions, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Social Security Act of 1935 created old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.

questions.q: Which English king was a leading commander of the Third Crusade?
questions.explain: Richard I ('the Lionheart') led the Third Crusade (1189-92), recapturing Acre and negotiating a truce with Saladin.

questions.q: Which ideology, emphasising class struggle and the abolition of private property, drew on the writings of Karl Marx?
questions.explain: Communism, rooted in Marx's analysis of class conflict, sought a classless society through the abolition of private property.

questions.q: Which Soviet economic body answered the Marshall Plan?
questions.explain: Comecon (1949) coordinated the economies of the Soviet bloc as a counter to Marshall aid.

questions.q: What document, proclaiming universal natural rights, did the National Assembly adopt in August 1789?
options: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
questions.explain: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was adopted on 26 August 1789, asserting liberty, equality and popular sovereignty.

questions.q: The Voting Rights Act, which banned literacy tests and protected black voter registration, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 outlawed discriminatory voting practices used against African Americans.

questions.q: Polish independence from communism was spearheaded by which trade union movement?
questions.explain: Solidarity, led by Lech Walesa, drove Poland's break from communist rule by 1989.

questions.q: In which year did the First Crusade capture Jerusalem?
questions.explain: The crusaders stormed and captured Jerusalem on 15 July 1099, establishing Christian rule in the Holy City.

questions.q: The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) was founded in which year?
questions.explain: The NAACP was founded in 1909 to combat racial discrimination and segregation.

questions.q: The 14th Amendment, granting citizenship and equal protection of the laws, was ratified in which year?
questions.explain: The 14th Amendment was ratified in 1868, defining citizenship and guaranteeing equal protection.

questions.q: In which year did Mussolini lead the March on Rome that brought him to power?
questions.explain: The Fascist March on Rome of October 1922 prompted King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint Mussolini Prime Minister.

questions.q: Medicare and Medicaid, providing health coverage for the elderly and poor, were established in which year?
questions.explain: Medicare and Medicaid were created in 1965 as part of Johnson's Great Society.

questions.q: The 19th Amendment, granting women the right to vote nationally, was ratified in which year?
questions.explain: The 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920, prohibiting denial of the vote on the basis of sex.

questions.q: At which 1187 battle did Saladin annihilate the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem?
questions.explain: At the Battle of Hattin (4 July 1187) Saladin destroyed the Frankish field army, leaving the kingdom defenceless.

questions.q: Malcolm X, the prominent Black nationalist who broke with the Nation of Islam, was assassinated in which year?
questions.explain: Malcolm X was assassinated in February 1965 in New York City.

questions.q: What was abolished by the National Assembly's decrees of 4-11 August 1789?
questions.explain: On the night of 4 August 1789 the Assembly abolished feudal privileges and seigneurial dues, dismantling the legal framework of the ancien regime.

questions.q: Which King of Scotland and England wrote the 1597 treatise Daemonologie?
questions.explain: James VI of Scotland (later James I of England) published Daemonologie in 1597, reflecting his interest in witchcraft.

questions.q: In which year did the USSR first test an atomic bomb, ending the US monopoly?
questions.explain: The Soviet Union detonated its first atomic bomb in 1949.

questions.q: Which US president labelled the USSR an 'evil empire' in 1983?
questions.explain: Ronald Reagan called the Soviet Union an 'evil empire' in 1983 during the Second Cold War.
